provenance: M41, postmortem shape S2 (`docs/evals/2026-08-24-demo-sec10k-inspector-postmortem.md` §1): at demo time the inspector's status line was a bare `<div id="banner">`, accessibility role `generic`, dropped by `observe.SKIP_ROLES` — the answer was not the accessible name of any element a plan could target. sec-10k-extract's legibility row (its build `6b37ffa99d05`) gave it `role="status" aria-label="doc_status"`. This case measures that the fix lands where it has to land: the observation the planner is shown carries `status — 'doc_status'`, and a plan naming it extracts the banner. Fixture is `src/browser/fixtures/sec10k-inspector.html`, a rendered snapshot of `https://whaleforce-sec10k.zeabur.app/?fixture=aapl-2025&run=1` taken 2026-08-26 against the build the page reported as `git_sha` `6b37ffa99d05` (see the build-provenance note at the end of this record — `/api/meta` was answering a different sha by `curl` at that moment), with `<script>`, the source `<iframe>` and the three Google Fonts `<link>` tags removed, so the page is static and the `fast` suite makes no network call. The font links were missed by the first capture pass and removed in a second: they are the reason to check a snapshot for outbound references rather than assume stripping scripts is enough. Removing them changes rendering only — the accessibility tree these cases grade is unaffected, and all five snapshot cases stayed green across the removal. Ground truth for the value is the inspector's own `/api/extract/fixture` (CLAUDE.md rule 6's per-site ground-truth endpoint, eval side only): `POST {"fixture":"aapl-2025"}` returns `doc_status: "success"`, `counts: {extracted: 18, incorporated_by_reference: 5}`, re-verified 2026-08-26. Watched RED first two ways: (1) with `expect.answer` set to a placeholder, `answer_matches: false`, reason `answer 'doc_status: success\n— 18 extracted · 5 incorporated_by_reference\nfixture: aapl-2025' != expected 'PLACEHOLDER'`; (2) with `role="status" aria-label="doc_status"` stripped from the fixture's banner — the pre-legibility shape — `failure:locate`, reason `step 3 (extract): relocation after locate failure: retargeting as {'text': 'doc_status'}; ResolveError: no tier resolved {'text': 'doc_status'}` — the relocation rung retargets on the name and the page has no such text, which is the demo shape itself (both cases go red this way). **Build provenance, corrected after cold review — three shas are involved and only two of them are the same thing.** `/api/meta` answered `5a44758598f5` when this milestone started and `6b37ffa99d05` at probe time. But the captured page's own footer — which the page fills from that same `/api/meta` field, one line of its own script — already read `build 6b37ffa99d05` in the FIRST capture, taken while `curl` to the same endpoint was still answering `5a44758598f5`. The two reads disagreed inside one session, which is what a rolling deploy across containers looks like; that explanation is INFERRED, not measured, and is written as an inference on purpose. What is measured: the committed snapshot is a capture of the build that reported itself as `6b37ffa99d05`, which is the same build ADR-030's probe ran against, so the fixture and the probe agree on one build rather than straddling two. The capture was re-taken later, after `/api/meta` had caught up, and diffed against the committed one — identical apart from a single `total_ms` figure inside the extraction evidence (227.6 -> 221.1), which is what that agreement looks like from the other side. The first version of this note claimed the capture was taken at `5a44758598f5`; the page says otherwise and the page is the artifact. Nothing in this repo reads either sha back — `tasks/TODO.md` T-M41-3 is the debt block for that, and D28's build-expiry rule is why it matters.

triage.note: This is the OFFLINE half. It cannot measure S1 (fetch-then-render), because a rendered snapshot is post-render by construction — S1 is measured live by `live-sec10k-authored-wait-reaches-the-doc-status`, whose `planner_saw.lacks` clause finds it unfixed by the deep link. (An earlier draft of this note named a case id that was never committed — the S1 claim was folded into the live pair instead of shipping a third, race-dependent live case; corrected after cold review.) The `planner_saw.lacks` clause is not decoration: the same observation does NOT reach the extracted-text region, and `sec10k-item-text-region-is-past-the-observation-cap` is the case for that.
